claims.statement: The Atlas handoff scope covers launch decisions, rollback operations, validation, and security readiness for the product-launch core audience.
ADR-017 records a single-writer cutover for the Atlas production launch.
The August 28 launch notes state that a dual-write interval may remain enabled through the first production hour.
Atlas rollback guidance is bound to the exact integrity of runbook v3.
Build 8841 is the current launch-gate validation record and reports no open severity-one validation findings.
Build 8702 remains indexed only as a stale, superseded validation record.
Security readiness cannot be represented beyond appendix metadata because authorized content access is unavailable.

decisions.statement: The Architecture Council recorded the single-writer cutover in ADR-017; the later launch-note conflict remains unresolved for human review.
The Atlas Launch Steering Group owns the go-live decision after validation, architecture, operations, and security blockers are reviewed.

duplicateGroups.reason: The two source records retain distinct locations but have the same immutable integrity; human review authorizes only the owned runbook as the canonical pointer.

gaps.description: The security appendix identity is authorized for metadata, but its content is unavailable to the collection and no excerpt permission exists.

reviewQuestions.question: Should the Architecture Council reaffirm ADR-017 or record a superseding decision for the launch-note dual-write interval?
Can Product Security provide an authorized current excerpt or a human-owned readiness statement for the restricted appendix?
Should Release Management extend the meeting-note retention period while the material architecture dispute remains open?

handoff.summary: The private local Atlas collection index is blocked for owner review by the unresolved write-path dispute and unavailable restricted security evidence; all source identities, stale context, and retention questions remain visible.
